view: First signs that compute is loosening at the short end, but not in long-term contracts. Looser: Anthropic not renewing ~50k H200s at SpaceX (re-marketed at ~$5/GPU-hr for early 2027), SpaceX cutting Blackwell spot to $10–12 from ~$15, the Ornn H100 index −10% m/m, 600MW+ of new short-tenor Nvidia AICP supply in 2027, and up to ~3 GW freed by the BIS remote-access rule. Still tight: CoreWeave and Oracle renewing old GPUs at 20–50% premiums, Silicon Data indexes at records, Vera Rubin signing at $7–9/hr. Watch: more Hopper non-renewals, the gap between spot and 1–3 year contract prices, and whether the price cuts reach Blackwell contracts.

events.lessor: Nvidia AICP partners (Firmus, Zankore, SharonAI, GMI, ChronoScale)
events.note: New sub-3-year GPU supply in 2027 is easing short-tenor rental prices; end offtake mostly 1–3 years. Nvidia has paused new AICP discussions.
Industry chatter: Anthropic not renewing; SpaceX marketing the capacity to other customers. Anthropic was 34.5% of SpaceX 3Q revenue, with 90-day cancellation rights after early-2027 lockups.
events.src: SemiAnalysis, "SpaceX Spot Prices Going Down, Anthropic Cancels H200 Clusters" (SB 70054)

events.note: In line with large-cluster pricing to Anthropic and Google. SA sees early signs of a broader cooldown, starting with H200 roll-offs.

events.event: Capacity freed by BIS remote-access rule
events.note: Needs a BIS license or new tenant; spot is only 1–2% of the market, so a small share of freed capacity could double spot supply. Well-built clusters may reprice higher with US labs.
GPUs fully paid off, so renewal revenue carries little debt service; mgmt sizes recontracting at ~$4B (2027) / ~$10B.
